transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2028-11-07 15:00 PT
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions), Ayan Patel (MerchantLabs CTO), Leah Kim (Head of Search), Mark Rivers (Infra), Sana Gomez (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
MerchantLabs probing Redwood hosting options for high-throughput embedding + rerank pipeline. Primary constraints: sub-120ms p50 for rerank stage, cost target < $0.0015/query, data residency + SOC2, option for private VPC or dedicated GPU pool. Discussed embedding dims (256 vs 1024), quantization tradeoffs, vector DB fanout/ hybrid rerank, and pilot scope. Next steps include sending pricing comparison, sample benchmark run, and private deploy deep-dive.

Topics: embeddings dimensionality; throughput & sharding; routing hosted vs dedicated vs private; security (SOC2, KMS, audit logs); SLA targets & pilot scope.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for carving time. i think we have about 40 minutes. quick intros?
[00:05] Ayan: sure I'm ayan, CTO at merchantlabs. we run search for merchant storefronts and catalogs.
[00:09] Leah: leah here, head of search, i own relevance and infra for reranking.
[00:12] Mark: mark infra, networking and security.
[00:14] Sana: sana product, coordinating pilot timeline.
[00:17] Sofia: great, from redwood we have daniel and priya, i'll pass to daniel to frame the options.
[00:22] Daniel: thanks. quick TLDR: we typically recommend three hosting paths — hosted api for fastest lift, dedicated capacity with reserved gpu pools for predictable throughput, and private (vpc/on-prem) for strict controls. for embeddings + rerank there's a common pattern: embeddings served, vector DB fanout, then rerank on a smaller set using a generative or cross-encoder. our differences show up in where you host each stage and how you batch/cache kvs.
[00:40] Leah: right, the big thing for us is latency on rerank. we need p50 under 120ms, p95 ideally < 350ms at 200 qps sustained. cost target is around $0.0015 per query end-to-end. is that realistic?
[00:56] Daniel: eee — it's tight but doable depending on model choice and where you run rerank. if rerank is on a 7B cross-encoder quantized and we use prefix caching / pipelined batching, p50 can be under 120 on dedicated gpus. hosted can hit similar numbers but you'd need a dedicated capacity commitment or predictable burst.
[01:18] Ayan: can you unpack the data flow? we currently compute 512-d embeddings, store in our vector DB (we use FaStIndex, internal name), we do a top-100 fanout and then re-rank top 10. looking to move to hybrid search later.
[01:32] Daniel: sure. common knobs: embedding dim (256 vs 512 vs 1024) — lower dims reduce vector db cost and fanout latency but might hurt recall. quantized embeddings can be compact. rerank model choice controls latency a lot — a cross-encoder vs a generative ranking step. also caching: prefix/kv cache can avoid repeated context recompute.
[01:52] Leah: our experiments show 512 dims with inner-product works ok but cost at our scale is high. curious about 256 dims and impact on relevance. do you have evals on dim dropoff?
[02:06] Priya: we ran customers on mixed dim strategies — in many ecommerce catalogs 256 dims with tuned retriever + product-specific rerank kept business metrics within 1-2% of baseline but cut cost ~30-40%. caveat: depends on product taxonomy and query distribution.
[02:24] Mark: security — we need SOC2, SAML SSO, and KMS integration. any issues with private deployment? we also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[02:35] Sofia: we have SOC2, plus our private deployment supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit log export. for hosted we provide tenant isolation, redwood can sign an MSA with addenda.
[02:48] Mark: fine. network wise we prefer VPC peering or AWS privatelink rather than public egress. does redwood support privatelink?
[02:55] Daniel: yes vpc peering and privatelink-like options in Dedicated/Private. hosted has secure endpoints but for the strictest network controls you move to Private.
[03:04] Sana: timeline — merchantlabs wants a pilot in 4–6 weeks if we line up. stakeholders include search eng, infra, and legal. pilot would be for live traffic on a subset of merchants.
[03:14] Sofia: okay good. question on traffic: what's your expected qps for pilot and full?
[03:19] Leah: pilot: 50 qps sustained, burst 200 qps. full: 400 qps sustained in peak region, multi-region later.
[03:27] Daniel: good to know. at 50 qps pilot you can test rerank latency and embedding pipeline with a small dedicated pool. for full 400 qps we'd recommend sharded dedicated capacity or private deployment across regions.
[03:39] Ayan: talk to me about fanout + vector DB costs. we currently do top-100, but we've considered a two-stage hybrid: top-200 dense + bm25 and then rerank top-10. we want to reduce vector DB ops.
[03:53] Daniel: two-stage hybrid is common — do an expanded fanout with cheap retriever then use learned rerank. you'll want to tune vector DB top-K to balance recall vs cost. sharding and locality can reduce tail latency.
[04:05] Leah: what about embedding storage skus? we host vectors in FaStIndex now but open to managed vector steps. does Redwood integrate with common vector DBs?
[04:14] Priya: we integrate with most — Faiss, Milvus, Pinecone, Weaviate, and custom setups. we don't replace your DB unless you want Redwood-managed vector storage. for many customers we do a hybrid: we host embeddings compute, push vectors to their DB, and run the rerank in Redwood.
[04:31] Mark: if we keep vectors on our side, how does network egress look? we can't have large egress bills.
[04:36] Daniel: you push embeddings over an internal link; for Dedicated/Private you can keep traffic inside your VPC or peered network. egress is only for external hosting. we can provide an estimate once we see payload sizes.
[04:49] Sana: okay, one of our constraints — PII retention rules: we can store embeddings for 30 days max, must be deletable on request. is that supported?
[04:58] Sofia: yes — retention policies and deletions are supported, plus audit logs for deletions. in Private you get direct control; in Hosted we provide API-driven deletion and retention settings.
[05:10] Ayan: model choices — what embedding models do you recommend? we have seen differences in semantic quality and costs.
[05:18] Daniel: we curate a model catalog. For cost-conscious pipelines: 256-d retrieval models (open models) plus a small cross-encoder for rerank. For highest quality, 1024-d retriever + larger reranker. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization or batching profiles based on your workload.
[05:34] Leah: about rerank model size — is a 7B cross-encoder enough vs a 70B generative step? we care about precision for purchase-intent queries.
[05:44] Priya: 7B cross-encoder with distillation often hits a sweet spot for many ecommerce signals; generative rerank adds latency and cost. customers who do personalized ranking sometimes use a cascade: fast 7B then optional gen step for long-tail.
[05:58] Mark: SLA — can we get an SLA for p95 latency? legal expects a number.
[06:03] Sofia: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in enterprise contracts. p95 guarantees are possible for specific routes with reserved capacity. we'll include suggested SLA wording in the pilot SOW.
[06:16] Ayan: our budget — important: what does dedicated cost monthly vs hosted pay-as-you-go?
[06:22] Sofia: i'll send a comparative spreadsheet — rough rule: hosted pay-as-you-go is higher per-query but no commit; dedicated has lower unit economics at a commit and predictable cost. Private has an infra + license cost profile. I'll include sample numbers for embedding + rerank per million queries.
[06:38] Leah: can we run an A/B where rewrite uses Redwood rerank vs our current infra? need to measure CTR and conversion impact.
[06:45] Daniel: absolutely, our Console supports per-route rollout and A/B. we'll instrument token-level cost and latency. we can also provide hooks for your analytics to pull traces or events.
[06:55] Sana: what about throttling and fallback — if dedicated is saturated, what's the behavior?
[07:00] Sofia: we have smart routing and fallbacks — can spill to hosted pools or to a lighter-weight model to keep the app live. you can set fallback policies per-route.
[07:10] Mark: we need to validate that fallback doesn't leak PII to third-party endpoints.
[07:14] Daniel: good point. fallbacks can be restricted to internal private pools only; if you choose hosted fallback, we can lock paths and ensure data masking or tokenization. we'll capture that in SOW.
[07:26] Ayan: benchmarks — we'd like Redwood to run our sample 100k queries and return latency/cost and quality metrics. is that doable?
[07:33] Daniel: yes, we typically run a benchmark. we'll need sample queries, a relevance goldset if you have one, and expected traffic profile. we can run both hosted and dedicated sims to compare.
[07:42] Leah: for the goldset, we have a labeled set of 5k queries with click labels. will that work?
[07:47] Priya: perfect. that'll let us compute nDCG and precision lift, and show the effect of emb dim and rerank model.
[07:56] Sana: timeline again — can you send pilot docs by friday? we want legal to start review.
[07:59] Sofia: yes, i'll send initial SOW + pricing + SOC2 and network playbook by Friday PST.
[08:06] Ayan: one technical deep question — how do you manage KV cache for rerank if we do user-personalization and need per-user state?
[08:13] Daniel: we support per-session KV cache, but personalization often requires routing consistency so the same shard serves a user's queries or we pass user embeddings at request time. lots of customers pass ephemeral user vectors and avoid long-lived per-user state for privacy.
[08:29] Leah: and for multi-region, how do you keep embedding consistency? concerns about vector drift if models upgraded.
[08:36] Priya: we version models and provide model pins per-route. upgrades are controlled via rollout policies — you can run canary traffic and compare eval sets. Redwood also stores model fingerprints so you can roll back.
[08:48] Mark: any gotchas on on-prem? our security team is sensitive about hardware and certs.
[08:53] Daniel: on-prem package includes certs, air-gap options, and support for customer HSMs. we do a joint runbook for upgrades. it's heavier lift but doable for regulated setups.
[09:06] Sana: pilot success criteria — what metrics should we agree on?
[09:09] Sofia: suggested: p50/p95 latency targets for rerank, nDCG improvement over baseline, cost per query, and stability (error rate < 0.1%). also integration completeness (VPC peering, SSO) and legal sign-off.
[09:23] Ayan: sounds right. can we aim to sign pilot MOU next week?
[09:27] Sofia: yes, i'll send the SOW to start the legal loop.
[09:30] Leah: small nit — how does Redwood support retraining or embedding refresh? we do monthly re-indexes and sometimes need realtime updates for inventory.
[09:39] Priya: we support incremental re-index and streaming ingestion; we recommend batch reindex for large changes and incremental for realtime updates. for embeddings, you can compute on your side and push or use Redwood compute.
[09:51] Mark: network again — please include egress cost estimate and privatelink steps in the doc.
[09:57] Daniel: will do.
[10:00] Sofia: ok wrapping up. recap of next steps — i'll send pricing/SOC2/SOW by Friday, daniel will run the sim once they share samples, mark to send network constraints, merchantlabs to confirm pilot qps and timeline. any other items?
[10:14] Ayan: no that's it. thanks.
[10:16] Sofia: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email.
